title_candidates: Samsung puts Gemini into everyday eyewear
summary: Samsung previewed Gemini-powered eyewear that can see, translate, navigate, and take notes. You can test the core camera workflow now with Gemini Live.

primary_source.title: Samsung Brings Galaxy Ecosystem Into Everyday Eyewear
primary_source.author: Samsung
key_facts: Samsung previewed intelligent eyewear developed with Gentle Monster and Warby Parker.
The eyewear combines a built-in camera, Gemini, Android XR, and Qualcomm's Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 chip.
Samsung demonstrated message summaries, live translation, note capture, navigation help, and live visual sharing.
Samsung claims up to nine hours of use per charge and up to seven additional recharges from the case.
Samsung did not announce a public price or firm sale date.

supporting_sources.title: Galaxy Unpacked July 2026 Highlights
key_facts: Samsung's event recap lists the intelligent eyewear among its July 2026 Galaxy announcements.

supporting_sources.title: Talk naturally with Gemini Live
key_facts: Gemini Live on Android can share a camera view or the device screen.
Screen sharing exposes the full screen and stops when the device is locked or the session is put on hold.
Shared content may be saved depending on the user's Gemini Apps Activity settings.

prerequisites: An Android phone or tablet with the Gemini app

steps.instruction: Review Gemini Apps Activity before sharing anything and choose a non-sensitive test.
Start Gemini Live, share the camera, and ask it to describe a household object while stating uncertainty.
Stop camera sharing and confirm that the camera indicator is no longer active.
Optionally share a dummy note, request a short summary, and stop sharing from Gemini or the Android notification.
Lock the screen to confirm sharing does not resume automatically, and get permission before including another person.
